source_text: Tunc Iacobo quoque in recordationem rediit quod hanc sibi significasset coronam diuinae dignationis ostensio. Nam superioribus diebus, cum eiusdem carrucae uehiculo Marianus et Iacobus et cum his ego uiam communiter carperemus, ad medium fere diem inter illa itineris confragosa mirabili et alto sopore correptus, postquam a nobis interpellatus et excitatus euigilat, Perturbatus sum, inquit, non sine gaudio meo, fratres; sed et uos mecum gaudere debetis. Uidi, inquit, iuuenem inenarrabili et satis ampla magnitudine, cuius uestitus discincta erat in tantum candida luce, ut oculi in eam constanter uidere non possent; cuius pedes terram non calcabant et uultus oris super nubes erat. Is cum transcurreret, unam tibi, Mariane, et unam mihi zonas purpureas in sinus nostros iaculatus est, et ait: Sequimini me cito. O quietem uigiliis omnibus fortiorem! O quietem quam feliciter dormiat quisquis in fide uigilat! Quae terrena tantum membra sopierat, quoniam uidere dominum nisi spiritus non ualebat. Quantum exultantes quamque sublimes animos martyrum fuisse credendum est, quibus in sancti nominis confessione passuris et audire Christum ante contigit et uidere offerentem se suis quocumque in loco, quocumque tempore. Non fuit inpedimento uehiculi se promouentis inquieta iactatio, nec dies medius, qui sub claro tunc sole fulgebat. Nulla noctis expectata secreta sunt: nouo genere gratiae martyri suo dominus nouum tempus uisionis elegit.
thought_title: James remembers his midday vision of purple sashes
orientation: James, the deacon fellow prisoner traveling with Marianus, now recalls a vision he had at midday while they rode together in the same cart.
pass_a_gloss: Then to James also into remembrance there came back that this crown to him had signified a showing of divine gracious favor. For in earlier days, when by the carriage of the same cart Marianus and James and with them I were together making the journey, toward almost the middle of the day among those rough places of the journey seized by a wonderful and deep sleep, after by us interrupted and roused he wakes, I have been disturbed, he said, not without my joy, brothers; but also you ought to rejoice with me. I saw, he said, a young man of unspeakable and quite great greatness, whose clothing loosened was white in so great light, so that eyes on it steadily to look were not able; whose feet the earth were not treading and the appearance of his face was above the clouds. He when he was passing through, one to you, Marianus, and one to me purple sashes into our laps he threw, and he said: Follow me quickly. O rest stronger than all keepings awake. O rest with which happily sleeps whoever in faith keeps awake. Which only earthly limbs had put to sleep, because to see the lord except spirit was not able. How exulting and how lifted up the souls of the martyrs must be believed to have been, to whom about to suffer in confession of faith of the holy name both to hear Christ before it befell and to see offering himself to his own in whatever place, in whatever time. Not was for hindrance the restless shaking of the vehicle moving itself forward, nor the middle of the day, which under a clear sun at that time was shining. No secret places of night were waited for: by a new kind of grace for his martyr the lord chose a new time of vision.

pass_b_english: Then James too remembered that a showing of divine gracious favor had marked out this crown for him. A few days earlier Marianus and James and I were riding together in the same cart. Toward midday, along the rough broken road, James was seized by a deep and wonderful sleep. When we called to him and roused him, he woke and said, "Brothers, I am shaken, but not without joy for me, and you ought to rejoice with me as well. I have seen," James said, "a young man of indescribable and very great stature. His loose robe shone with so white a light that eyes could not look steadily at it. His feet did not touch the ground, and his face stood above the clouds. As he swept past, he threw one purple sash into your fold, Marian, and one into mine, and said, 'Follow me quickly.'"
O sleep stronger than all watching! O sleep in which whoever stays awake in faith sleeps so happily! It had put to sleep only his earthly limbs, for only the spirit could see the Lord.

How exultant and how lifted up the hearts of the martyrs must have been. They were about to suffer in confession of faith of the holy name, yet they were already granted both to hear Christ beforehand and to see Him offering Himself to His own in every place and at every time. The restless jolting of the moving cart was no hindrance, nor was the midday then blazing under a bright sun. They waited for no secrecy of night: with a new kind of grace the Lord chose a new time of vision for His martyr.
